pages.wrong_reason: The edge {MPC} ⇒ OT attributed to BH26 does not match BH26. The paper introduces oblivious interactive hash functions (OIHFs) and proves OIHF ⇒ OT via a non-black-box reduction (abstract, mirrored on the wiki's BH26 page and confirmed by web search): the hypothesis is OIHF, not MPC, and the migrated bullet's 'in a black-box way' contradicts the paper's 'non-black-box'. The qualifier 'for certain non-trivial functionalities' is an undefined side condition the hyperedge cannot carry. General MPC ⇒ OT is trivial (a protocol for every functionality computes the OT functionality — folklore); 'secure computation of a single non-trivial functionality ⇒ OT' is the completeness line of Kilian (STOC 1991, STOC 2000) and Beimel–Malkin–Micali (CRYPTO 1999), not BH26. The OIHF ⇒ OT edge already exists as oihf-to-ot-bh26; an unattributed folklore mpc-to-ot page is optional.

sources.ref_file_title: BGKPS14 - Protecting Obfuscation against Algebraic Attacks
sources.authors: Boaz Barak, Sanjam Garg, Yael Tauman Kalai, Omer Paneth, Amit Sahai
sources.note: VBB security of a simplified branching-program obfuscator in a generic multilinear-map (ideal graded-encoding) model. Verified: cryptobib EC:BGKPS14 (LNCS 8441 pp. 221-238, DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-55220-5_13); eprint 2013/631 and abstract via web search.

pages.class_justification: GGHRSW13 give a candidate: no security reduction from a stated multilinear-map assumption exists, so there is no reduction to place in the RTV taxonomy.
pages.model_justification: The candidate is stated in the standard model but has no proof there; GGHRSW13's own argument for the NC1 core and BGKPS14's VBB proof live in idealized generic-encoding models, a separate model-scoped edge.
pages.statement: The first candidate [[indistinguishability-obfuscation|iO]] for all polynomial-size circuits, from candidate [[multilinear-maps|multilinear maps]] (graded encodings): a core obfuscator for NC$^1$ built from graded encodings, bootstrapped to all circuits with leveled fully homomorphic encryption. No reduction from a standard-model multilinear-map assumption is given; the NC$^1$ core is argued secure only in an idealized generic model of encoded matrices — [[GGHRSW13 - Candidate indistinguishability obfuscation and functional encryption for all circuits|GGHRSW13]].
pages.sketch: The core obfuscator turns an NC$^1$ circuit into a matrix branching program via Barrington's theorem, rerandomizes it Kilian-style, and publishes the matrices under a graded encoding; evaluation multiplies the input-selected encodings and zero-tests the product. Obfuscating the NC$^1$ circuit that checks a low-depth proof of correct homomorphic evaluation and then decrypts bootstraps the construction to all polynomial-size circuits.
pages.improvements_text: - A simplified branching-program variant of the NC$^1$ obfuscator is virtual-black-box secure, hence iO-secure, in a generic multilinear-map (ideal graded-encoding) model — [[BGKPS14 - Protecting Obfuscation against Algebraic Attacks|BGKPS14]]
notes_to_keep: Candidate construction, not a proven reduction from a stated assumption; many of the underlying multilinear-map candidates have since been attacked.

Bootstrapping uses leveled FHE (instantiable from LWE), an additional hypothesis the edge does not carry.
Hypothesis wikilink multilinear-maps has no page; still true after this pass.

pages.wrong_reason: 'Every NIZK scheme gives a non-interactive commitment' is false as stated. The wiki defines NIZK per language, and every language in BPP has a trivial unconditional NIZK (the verifier decides membership itself) that yields no commitment; commitments imply one-way functions, so the unqualified implication would build OWFs from nothing. The true results carry a hardness qualifier on the language: in the public-parameter model, one-way functions are necessary for computational NIZK for hard-on-average languages (Pass–shelat, 'Unconditional Characterizations of Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge', CRYPTO 2005, LNCS 3621 pp. 118-134), and OWFs give Naor commitments, non-interactive in the CRS model — a composite chain repo policy splits into separate pages. The correct edge, if wanted, is 'NIZK for a hard-on-average language ⇒ OWF' (PS05), not NIZK ⇒ COM.
flags: If the corrected edge is created, verify the exact PS05 theorem (public- vs secret-parameter model, proofs vs arguments, hard-on-average hypothesis) with paper access. Bibliographic data confirmed in cryptobib (C:Passhe05, CRYPTO 2005 pp. 118-134); the necessity direction was confirmed only via web-search snippets (iacr.org and Springer egress-blocked).
The migration note's SUSPECT MATH flag on this page is confirmed correct.

sources.ref_file_title: GHJS25 - Public-Key Encryption from Planted Clique and Noisy k-LIN Over Expanders
sources.authors: Riddhi Ghosal, Isaac M. Hair, Aayush Jain, Amit Sahai
sources.note: Verified: cryptobib STOC:GHJS25 (pp. 1921-1932, DOI 10.1145/3717823.3718306); abstract via web search.

pages.class_justification: The paper does not classify its reduction in RTV terms and the construction could not be inspected from this environment; recording a class would be a guess.
pages.model_justification: Standard-model construction; no idealized oracle appears in the abstract or in any of the four migrated statements.
pages.statement: If the [[planted-clique|planted clique]] conjecture holds against $n^{\log^\alpha n}$-time adversaries for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$, and [[noisy-k-lin-over-expanders|noisy $k$-LIN]] holds over $(\gamma, \Omega(\log n), 2^{(\log n)^\alpha})$-expanding matrices over $\FF_p$, then there is a [[public-key-encryption|PKE]] scheme semantically secure against non-uniform polynomial-size circuits — [[GHJS25 - Public-Key Encryption from Planted Clique and Noisy k-LIN Over Expanders|GHJS25]], Theorem 5.12.
notes_to_keep: Genuinely conjunctive: both hypotheses are required together; the edge must not be split into two single-hypothesis reductions.
The adversary classes differ on the two sides: quasi-polynomial hardness is assumed of planted clique, while the resulting PKE is secure against non-uniform polynomial-size circuits.
flags: The migrated glosses say planted clique 'against sub-exponential adversaries'; the abstract (web-search snippet of eprint 2025/1501 and the STOC page) says $n^{\log^\alpha n}$ hardness for any $\alpha \in (0,1)$, which is quasi-polynomial ($2^{\log^{1+\alpha} n}$), not sub-exponential in the $2^{n^\epsilon}$ sense. The statement follows the abstract; confirm the exact adversary class of Theorem 5.12 with paper access.

The expander parameters $(\gamma, \Omega(\log n), 2^{(\log n)^\alpha})$ and the theorem number come from the wiki's reference-page abstract and the migrated bullets only; no accessible host exposed them (eprint, ACM DL, Semantic Scholar egress-blocked).

The GHJS25 reference page's abstract on the wiki misreads $n^{\log^\alpha n}$ as the planted clique SIZE (impossible: it exceeds $n$); it is the adversary runtime bound. Reference-page fix is outside this batch; send to the skeptical-checker.
The paper also gives an alternative construction from a search variant of noisy $k$-LIN (Theorem 8.8) — same paper, no separate improvement entry.

flag added: expander parameters and theorem number confirmed only from wiki-internal text

pages.wrong_reason: The page records kind: equivalence with hypothesis NP and conclusion coNP, i.e. it asserts NP = coNP. That equality is a major open problem, not a theorem, and is widely conjectured false (NP = coNP would collapse the polynomial hierarchy to its first level). The migrated prose only defines coNP as the complement class of NP — a definitional duality (coNP = {L : complement of L is in NP}), not a class equality — and the migration note itself says this wants a 'complement-of' edge type, not a reduction. There is no correct reduction edge to substitute; the page should be deleted or converted to a non-hyperedge note on the coNP page.
flags: HIGH: the page as it stands asserts NP = coNP, a false-as-far-as-known claim in the relations graph. Recommend deletion; the definitional relationship already lives in the coNP page's intro prose.

sources.note: Defines PP (with BPP and ZPP). Bibliographic data confirmed via the DBLP search snippet (SIAM J. Comput. 6(4): 675-695, 1977). The attribution of NP ⊆ PP to this paper rests on search snippets (Complexity Zoo 'Defined in [Gil77]', a historical survey crediting Gill with NP ⊆ PP and closure under complement); DBLP, doi.org, Wikipedia and Zoo mirrors are egress-blocked. pages.class_justification: Proven unconditional containment between complexity classes; repo convention assigns class: free.
pages.statement: $\classNP \subseteq \classPP$: every language in [[nondeterministic-polynomial-time|NP]] is in [[probabilistic-polynomial-time|PP]] — [[Gil77 - Computational complexity of probabilistic Turing machines|Gil77]].
pages.sketch: The $\classPP$ machine flips one coin: on heads it accepts; on tails it samples a uniform candidate witness $w \in \bits^m$ and accepts iff the NP verifier accepts $w$. The acceptance probability is $1/2 + a/2^{m+1}$, with $a$ the number of accepting witnesses, which exceeds $1/2$ exactly on yes-instances.
notes_to_keep: The proof gloss on the PP page ('accept iff strictly more than half the nondeterministic paths lead to accepting') is wrong without padding, since a yes-instance may have a single accepting path; the inclusion itself is correct.
